<!-- pr-reviewer: 7efea82464d78c31a5d7d63754744c8e25ba5997 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Deciding review (safety tier: tessellation feeds toolpath and gouge checks), made on top of the earlier first pass at the same head. Trial-merged with current `main`: clean, no conflicts. Built locally, in release.

**What looks good**
- The certified bound is sound and over-estimates. For a triangle with corner points p_k, footpoints f_k = S(q_k) at distance d_k, and q(b) the barycentric mix of the q_k, the point-to-surface distance of T(b) is at most |T(b) - S(q(b))|. That is at most max d_k + eps, where eps >= |S(q(b)) - sum b_k S(q_k)|. `tri_metrics` returns `dmax + eps` (`mesh_deviation.rs`). Any sample whose projection is not yet done uses the parametric distance at the hint. That is only larger than the true projection distance, so it errs in the safe direction.
- eps is the Peano/Taylor remainder, 1/8 (Muu du^2 + 2 Muv du dv + Mvv dv^2) (`mesh_bound_spline.rs` `nurbs_eps`, `revolved_eps`). The 1/8 follows from the variance bound du^2/4 on the barycentric spread. Derivative bounds come from Bezier hodograph control differences (convex hull) after de Boor blossom restriction (Farin; Piegl and Tiller, *The NURBS Book*), and from the quotient rule for the rational case. C^0 knots (multiplicity = p) and closed seams add `0.25 * jump * du`, the interpolation error of a derivative kink. Multiplicity > p refuses. I checked this by hand.
- I checked it independently with a throwaway fuzz test, not committed. It covered about 23,000 random NURBS surfaces: degrees 1-3 in both directions, rational weights, kinked knot vectors, and triangles up to the full domain with 861 dense samples each. There were no violations (worst d/eps = 1 + 1.5e-12, which is roundoff). The first run did flag a "violation", but only with triangles outside the surface domain, which a face mesh never has. Clamped to the domain, there were none.
- Refinement is sound as a decision procedure (`subtri_bound`). It stops only when the bound is <= the running gate or <= tol, or at depth 3 (N = 32). If it stops at depth 3 with the bound above tol, the mesh is refused, never passed. A triangle whose corner distances already exceed tol is not refined and is refused.
- No mesh gets coarser: `PLAN_MARGIN` only multiplies the chord by 0.5, floored at `size * MIN_TOL_FRACTION`. The replan happens once and the tolerance stays the requested one.
- Degenerate splines refuse by name. `parametric_eps` returning None (bad knots, n <= p, zero or negative weights, non-finite values, a ctrl count mismatch, a multiplicity above p) becomes `Unmeasured::NoPoint`, then `MeshRefusal::Unmeasured`. Depth and replans are bounded, and `stop` is polled per 256 triangles and per refinement. I found no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new src (the only hits are in `#[cfg(test)]`). Indexing is guarded by checked sizes, with `.get` used for node access.
- No new `camcraft-*` dependency, no Cargo, `build.rs`, `.github` or process-file changes. The decision file `docs/decisions/1029-...md` is present and complete. Provenance lines are present on the new modules.

**Results (locally, on this machine, release profile, merged with main)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --lib` | 3 passed |
| `--test machining_mesh` | 7 passed |
| `--test machining_mesh_bounds` | 4 passed |
| `--test machining_mesh_shortfalls` | 3 passed, 1 ignored. The ignored one is `provoke_face_capped_note`; run with `--ignored`, it passes. |
| `--test step_agreement` | 18 passed |
| `--test mesh_deviation_bench -- --ignored` | 1 passed |
| `cargo clippy --release -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Goldens and mesh counts**
- No golden and no snapshot PNG changed. The PR body says "Goldens moved: none".
- Behaviour change, explained: the Solidcraft sample at 0.1 mm used to refuse. It now meshes after the 0.05 mm replan, because the spline faces are judged by the projected bound instead of the over-reading parametric distance. The test pins this (`parametric > 0.1`, `largest() <= 0.1`) and a crafted un-reducible spline bump still refuses. This is accepted: the certified bound is what justifies the pass.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The bound certifies triangle-to-surface distance only. Surface-to-triangle (mesh cutting off a peak) is not covered. This is the same for the analytic faces as before, and the trim is still unchecked. It may be worth an issue if it is not already tracked.
2. `mesh_deviation.rs` and the new bound files exceed ~400 lines. This is growth, not blocking.
3. The fuzz above ran as a throwaway outside the PR. A small randomized soundness test in the repo would guard the blossom and jump code against later edits.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
